arguments.value:
This agreement is between Go Call, Inc. and PageMaster Corporation for a promotion in which PageMaster would offer free new Motorola Wordline Alphanumeric (or equal) pagers with no activation fee to customers who buy 12 months of numeric paging and airtime service from PageMaster. Customers had to prepay 12 months of local numeric airtime at $10.33 per month through a designated nationwide airtime provider, and also pay shipping, handling, and applicable sales taxes. The promotion was to run from June 1, 1999 to June 1, 2000, with a possible one-year extension if 3,000 pagers per month were distributed to purchase customers.

PageMaster was responsible for setting up and maintaining a toll-free number for the promotion, providing between 100,000 and 500,000 pagers, handling fulfillment and customer complaints, contracting with a nationwide airtime provider (MetroCall Inc. was selected for this purpose where available and authorized), and providing programming software so Go Call could broadcast messages of 125 characters or less to customers who redeemed pagers. PageMaster also agreed not to run the same or a similar promotion with any other On-Line Casinos from June 1, 1999 through June 1, 2000.

Go Call was responsible for preparing and paying for the advertising materials and submitting all artwork and advertising to PageMaster for approval, and it agreed not to run the same or similar promotions during the term with any other entity providing paging services, equipment, or related products and services. Go Call was also to provide a $100,000 deposit when the agreement was executed to secure pager availability; PageMaster would refund $1 per pager delivered, up to $100,000, with monthly accounting. PageMaster also agreed to pay Go Call co-op marketing funds of $3 per pager and 5% of airtime renewal revenue for each pager redeemed under the promotion.

The agreement requires prior approval of advertising and trademark use, contains mutual indemnity provisions, limits liability, and allows termination or suspension for force majeure events. It states that California law governs the agreement and that Los Angeles County, California is the exclusive venue for disputes, with negotiations followed by binding arbitration if needed. The agreement also requires written notices, confidentiality of information exchanged for the promotion, and says it would be terminated if not signed and delivered by March 26, 1999.
